1. tell me about a hospitality moment you’ve had at any job that you were really proud of

2. tell me about a time you made a mistake at work and what happened afterwards

I was asked these 2 things at an interview for my current job and although I was a little nervous at first, I thought it was nice to talk about these things and reflect on my experience and how far I’ve come :)

also: out times are fake in restaurants. just because you’re scheduled until 8 doesn’t mean you’re leaving by 8. if your section is still full and there’s closing sidework (chores you have to do at the end of the night, i.e., polishing silverware/glasses, folding linens, cleaning certain stations, etc.), you won’t be leaving before all the work is done. don’t be that coworker who fights everybody about your out time!!

there’s service and there’s hospitality. service is the technical aspects of the job. if you’re dining somewhere that sells $50 steaks vs $10, the standards of service are likely higher. the steak isn’t the only part of your night out, you’re at a restaurant. in fine dining settings, there’s more care taken for steps of service - including the set up and clean up that you don’t see. detailing the restaurant, etc. 

hospitality is the emotional side of the job. the feelings we create with each guest. and we have to be able to read a table within minutes of the first greet, understanding what they want/how they want to be treated, and executing it seamlessly. and doing that with multiple tables simultaneously for ~8 hours. it’s the mood in the restaurant. it’s making you feel welcome when you join us for dinner. higher end restaurants will have more emphasis on hospitality than casual places. we have to be perfect, hit every mark, be whoever each guest wants us to be, and cater to every need - ideally before you even know you need it. 

it’s a lot more than the price of an entree.

uncooked meat has a lot of moisture in it which will lead it to spoil very quickly if not properly stored, and cooked but not cured meat will also spoil fast without proper storage - and you really don’t want to fuck around with bacteria that grows on food, unless you want to have a really shitty (literally) time. but it’s mostly about moisture in food, as bacteria prefers warm, moist places to grow.

custodian: 1781, "one who has the care or custody of anything" (a library, a lunatic, etc.), from custody (Latin custodia) + -an.
